title: Efficient Algorithms for TURF Analysis
text: Fast TURF (total unduplicated reach frequency) analysis. turf() finds combinations products reach respondents. builds combination batches, refined swap searches, rather scoring every possible combination. search implemented Rust via savvy.

title: Efficient Algorithms for TURF Analysis
text: Building source requires Rust toolchain (cargo rustc). Install https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install, :
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("Adam-Hubbs/y2turf")

title: Efficient Algorithms for TURF Analysis
text: Activation data one row per respondent one column per product, 1 respondent activated product 0 otherwise. package includes simulated example, . result one row per combination, best first, products, total_reach, total_frequency. See ?turf search works arguments trade speed thoroughness.
code: library(y2turf)  turf(   am,   possible_products = colnames(am),   num_products = 4,   batch_size = 2,   keep_n_at_batch = 10,   num_return = 3 )

title: Efficient Algorithms for TURF Analysis
text: Rust source lives src/rust/src/. R/000-wrappers.R, src/init.c, src/rust/api.h generated , don’t edit hand. changing #[savvy] function’s signature docs, run savvy::savvy_update() regenerate bindings, devtools::document(). Build R (devtools::document(), devtools::load_all(), devtools::install()), bare cargo build, lacks environment R’s build tools provide. cargo clippy cargo fmt fine. Builds always use release profile, timings reflect real performance. Set SAVVY_PROFILE=dev debug build. clean build, delete src/rust/target. Don’t use devtools::clean_dll(): deletes compiled files inside src/rust/target cargo doesn’t know rebuild, next build fails “find native static library unwind_protect”. Deleting src/rust/target fixes .

title: Run a TURF analysis — turf
text: TURF (total unduplicated reach frequency) analysis looks combination num_products products reaches respondents, respondent reached activated (choose) least one product combination. turf() returns best num_return combinations. Scoring every combination quickly becomes infeasible: 53 products 886 million combinations 8. Instead, turf() builds combinations batches repairs local swap search, scoring small fraction combinations. usually finds best combination, unless batch_size = num_products guaranteed . sections explain step.

title: Run a TURF analysis — turf
text: show_combinations = TRUE, turf() reports many combinations scored. Regular combinations scored batches: batch, choose(remaining products, batch size). Swap combinations generated swap searches, duplicates removed within round across rounds.

title: Run a TURF analysis — turf
text: batch_size matters . Larger batches look ahead, less likely lock poor choice, batch_size = num_products scores every combination, guaranteeing best result. cost grows fast: batch scores choose(remaining products, batch_size) combinations (see ). use_swaps repairs poor choices made earlier batches, usually small cost. keep_n_at_batch gives swap search starting points, small cost. swap_top_n widens swap search, explores alternatives stopping. round scores swap_top_n * k * (n - k) combinations k n products. Combinations size among 53 products: practical approach start small batches swaps, check whether larger batches (larger swap_top_n) change result.

Shared work. batch's combinations visited depth first, lexicographic order, carrying products chosen far. {, b} computed shared every {, b, ...} , combination costs single count, whatever size:   Bounded memory. Combinations never stored bulk. one scored visited, best kept, fixed-size heap. work split across threads first product, swaps also scored parallel.
